column1: # boru Language Specification: Function VALUES at the pointer dispatch like words
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# A Function value that reaches the pointer (typically a `get` result — a
# map field, a module export) dispatches with the same forward+stack
# matching as a named word (the unified collection rule). Historically a
# non-anonymous `fn` value whose match needed FORWARD tokens silently
# stayed on the stack as data while the equivalent afn lambda dispatched
# (the F4 finding, design/MINILANG.0.md §10); execFnDefLiteral now routes
# such a match through forward parking and re-processes it against the
# stack. No-match cases still leave the value as data, and macro values
# stay data (lang/spec/macro.tsv §5).
# §1  forward dispatch of stored fn values
def m {f: (fn [[a:Integer][Integer][a add 1]])}  m.f 5
column3: a stored fn collects its forward arg like a word

column1: def m {f: (fn [[a:Integer][Integer][a add 1]])}  5 m.f
column3: stack form (mirror equivalence)

column1: def m {f: (fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][(a mul 100) add b]])}  m.f 2 3
column3: two forward args bind in sig order

column1: def m {f: (fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][(a mul 100) add b]])}  3 m.f 2
column3: mixed form: sig[0] forward, sig[1] stack

column1: def m {f: ([a:Integer] => [a add 1])}  m.f 5
column3: afn parity — lambdas dispatched this way already

column1: # §2  module exports — fn values exported by inline modules call like words
import module [export "X" {f: (fn [[a:Integer][Integer][a add 1]])}]  X.f 5
column3: a module-exported fn collects forward args

column1: import module [import "boru:string-util" export "X" {up: (fn [[s:String][String][StringUtil.upper s]])}]  X.up 'ab'
column3: the export body runs in MODULE scope (module-private import resolves)

column1: # §3  negatives — no match leaves the value as data; module scope is sealed
def m {f: (fn [[a:Integer][Integer][a add 1]])}  m.f
column3: bare value, no args: stays data

column1: def m {f: (fn [[a:Integer][Integer][a add 1]])}  m.f 'x'
column3: type mismatch: no dispatch — the fn stays data, 'x' strands on top

column1: import "boru:string-util"  import module [export "X" {up: (fn [[s:String][String][StringUtil.upper s]])}]  X.up 'ab'
column3: an OUTER import does not leak into the module body's scope

column1: # §4  a paren expression resolving to a FUNCTION WORD never induces a call
#     (NUR035). `Mod.word arg` lowers to `( Mod dot word ) arg`, so the
#     resolved fn value lands alone inside a synthetic group with its
#     argument on the far side of the close paren — a forward-scan boundary
#     — and the open paren barring a prefix operand the other way. The group
#     RESOLVES the word; the call belongs to whatever encloses it. Before
#     this, dispatch happened inside the group against an argument window
#     that is empty by construction, so a word with a 0-arg overload matched
#     THAT and its arg-taking signatures were unreachable — silently, as a
#     wrong value rather than an error.
#     A group the USER wrote is unaffected: `(g)` still means "call g".
#     Only the reach lowering's own group is tagged (expandReach).
import module [ def w fn [[] [String] ["zero"]  [x:String] [String] [x]] export "M" {w: w/v} ] end  M.w "one"
column3: forward form reaches the ARG-TAKING signature of a mixed-arity module export

column1: import module [ def w fn [[] [String] ["zero"]  [x:String] [String] [x]] export "M" {w: w/v} ] end  "one" M.w
column3: and so does the stack form — the open paren no longer hides the prefix operand

column1: import module [ def w fn [[] [String] ["zero"]  [x:String] [String] [x]] export "M" {w: w/v} ] end  M.w
column3: with no argument the 0-arg signature still answers, one step later

column1: import module [ def w fn [[] [String] ["zero"]  [x:String] [String] [x]] export "M" {w: w/v} ] end  size (M.w)
column3: and a user paren around the bare form still dispatches inside it, so a consumer receives the RESULT

column1: # §4b a paren PLACES its collapsed Function value — it never re-steps it
#     (NUR073, discharged 2026-08-24 by the BROAD verdict's clause-3 fix:
#     "parens do not re-step; they place a value or values on the forward
#     stack"). This is the row the record could not pin while its oracle
#     was open, and it is pinned through `canon` / `typeof` rather than on
#     the bare residual, because a name-rendering difference survives in
#     the residual renderer (the interpreter's value carries the resolved
#     PARAM name, the compiler's the defining name) — NUR074's class, not
#     this one's.
#     Note what is NOT affected: a bare WORD inside a group still calls
#     (`(g)` dispatches g during the group's own evaluation — §4 above),
#     and a reach-lowered group still dispatches (dot access, MathUtil.sqrt).
#     Only a Function VALUE that survives the collapse is placed.
def z fn [[][Integer][42]]  def h fn [[f:Function][Any][f/v]]  canon ((h z/v))
column3: the nested group places the returned fn — canon agrees on both engines (NUR073's discharge row)

column1: def z fn [[][Integer][42]]  def h fn [[f:Function][Any][f/v]]  typeof ((h z/v))
column3: …and so does typeof: the value divergence is closed

column1: def z fn [[][Integer][42]]  (z/v) apply
column3: the placed value still fires where an application is ASKED for

column1: # §5  a failed dispatch is LOUD, wherever the value would have gone
#     (design/legacy/FN-VALUE-DISPATCH.0.ignore). The old contract marked the value
#     and let the end-of-run drain judge it, so any consumer at all — a
#     `print`, a `def`, an Any slot — silenced a real dispatch failure.
#     The judgement is now made where the call is, so what happens to the
#     value afterwards cannot change the verdict. `/v` is how a caller
#     says the function IS the value it wanted.
#     The §3 rows above stay as they are: those fn values are ANONYMOUS,
#     and an anonymous value with no matched positions is data by
#     construction. This section is about NAMED functions — a module
#     export, a `def`ed fn, a `usurp`ed value — which is where a call was
#     meant.
#     Raising at the SITE also makes the failure CATCHABLE — a `do […] error
#     […]` around the call traps it like any other error, where the old
#     end-of-run drain fired outside every handler. That is pinned as a Go
#     test (lang/go/fnvalue_loud_dispatch_test.go) rather than a row here:
#     check mode evaluates a code body's parens on its own straight line, so
#     it reports the call as an error while the run traps it, and a row would
#     read as a checker false positive. The divergence is pre-existing and
#     unchanged by this contract (design/legacy/FN-VALUE-DISPATCH.0.ignore §6).
import module [ def w fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [x]] export "M" {w: w/v} ] end  M.w "x"
column3: a named export called with a mismatched arg raises AT THE CALL

column1: import module [ def w fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [x]] export "M" {w: w/v} ] end  print (M.w "x")
column3: and a consumer around it does not silence it — the old drain never fired here

column1: import module [ def w fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [x]] export "M" {w: w/v} ] end  def y (M.w "x")  y
column3: nor does binding the result with def

column1: import module [ def w fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [x]] export "M" {w: w/v} ] end  M.w
column3: a bare reference with no argument is still a VALUE, not a call

column1: import module [ def w fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [x]] export "M" {w: w/v} ] end  M.w/v
column3: /v means "the function is what I want" — no dispatch, no error

column1: import module [ def w fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [x]] export "M" {w: w/v} ] end  def g M.w/v  g 5
column3: and the parked value is still callable, which is what a caller wanted it for

column1: # §6  a value-called dispatch SEALS at collection completion (NUR038).
#     Completing a forward collection re-steps the callee stack-only — the
#     /s rewrite named words get (forceStackWord). A function VALUE has no
#     WordInfo to stamp, so before the seal the re-step re-planned
#     forward-first: a completed Any window stayed open, reached across the
#     statement boundary, claimed the NEXT statement's tokens (its dot-read
#     fn value included), bound the LAST arrival, stranded the earlier
#     collects, and ran side effects in reverse — silently, exit 0. The
#     engine now (1) seals a completed value-called collection with a
#     one-shot stack-only re-step, and (2) treats a reach-read named fn
#     that WOULD COLLECT as a barrier at arrival (committing the pending
#     window as `end` would — commitBarrierForward — or resolving it from
#     the stack), so consecutive value-called statements each bind their
#     own arguments. Print-order and zero-return twins are pinned in
#     lang/go/test/nur038_seal_test.go (a TSV row can't assert stdout
#     order, and the `m.p typeof` strict "still waiting" twin is a Go
#     test there too — the compiled path models that window differently,
#     the pre-existing check-vs-run class §5 already notes); the
#     twin-call VALUE rows live in
#     lang/spec/frontier/frontier-nur038-seal.tsv — semantically green,
#     compile-declined on the pre-existing residual-ordering limitation
#     ("dynamic value precedes residual args"). The EXPLICIT-PAREN row of
#     that set GRADUATED here 2026-08-27 (Stage 3): each paren applies and
#     nets one value, and the residual layout no longer reads two placed
#     results as an auto-dispatch hazard, because the collapse now records
#     which values a rewind re-steps (design/PAREN-RESTEP-RULE.0.md).
def f fn [[x:Any] [Any] [x]] end def m {p: f/v} end m.p 5 add 1
column3: a sealed call composes with a following word statement

column1: def f fn [[x:Any] [Any] [x]] end def m {p: f/v} end (m.p 5) (m.p 7)
column3: explicit parens as the seal — graduated from the frontier 2026-08-27

column1: def i fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [x add 1]] end def m {i: i/v} end m.i 5 m.i 7
column3: typed twins — the type gate already isolated these; unchanged

column1: #     Six more twin-call rows GRADUATED 2026-09-05 out of that frontier
#     file: a user call's single result is PARKED data where it lands
#     (design/PAREN-RESTEP-RULE.0.md, the bare-call rows), so two dynamic
#     results in one residual are two placed values, not an auto-dispatch
#     hazard — the residual lowering now lays them out as such.
def f fn [[x:Any] [Any] [x]] end def m {p: f/v} end m.p 5 m.p 7
column3: consecutive Any-param value calls each bind their own arg

column1: def f fn [[x:Any] [Any] [x]] end def m {p: f/v} end m.p 1 m.p 2 m.p 3
column3: three in a row — every window closes at its own statement

column1: def g fn [[a:Any b:Any] [Any] [(a mul 100) add b]] end def m {g: g/v} end m.g 1 2 m.g 3 4
column3: two-arg windows close at their own arity, not at the next call

column1: import module [def p fn [[x:Any] [Any] [x]] export "M" {p: p/v}] end M.p 5 M.p 7
column3: module-export twins seal identically (the original NUR038 shape)

column1: def f fn [[x:Any] [Any] [x]] end def h fn [[y:Any] [Any] [y]] end def m {p: f/v} end m.p 5 h 7
column3: value call then bare-word call (the word barrier, unchanged)

column1: def f fn [[x:Any] [Any] [x]] end def m {p: f/v} end m.p 5 end m.p 7
column3: explicit `end` as the seal (unchanged)

column1: # §7  fn-local fns as higher-order body words FAIL TO COMPILE compilation (NUR037).
#     A fn bound by `def … fn` INSIDE another fn and then NAMED as a
#     code-body word (`for-each [step] xs`) resolves per run through the
#     def stack, which a compiled program never populates — the enclosing
#     body's def is compiled away — so every record-time admission that
#     baked the NAME (the island span, the CALL_NATIVE const-bake, the
#     closure probe) turned a working program into undefined_word in the
#     DEFAULT mode only. bodyRefsFnLocalFn (eng/go/carrier.go) now declines
#     the whole program at compile admission, and it is then silently
#     re-run on the interpreter (design/COMPILABLE-SUBSET.md §5) — an open
#     defect, not a sanctioned outcome. The declining
#     shapes are pinned in lang/go/test/nur037_fnlocal_test.go — a spec
#     value row must compile (failureCeiling 0). The rows here pin the
#     twins the compile failure must NEVER over-match, holding both engines to
#     them through the differential gate: module-scope callbacks (the
#     utils house-rule shape) and a fn-local VALUE read (the closure
#     path's lexical capture).
def stp fn [[e:Integer] [Integer] [e add 1]] end each [stp] [1 2]
column3: a module-scope fn named as an each body word keeps compiling

column1: def acc (flex {}) end def stp fn [[e:String] [Any] [acc set (e) true]] end for-each [stp] ['x' 'y'] end acc
column3: a module-scope fn as a for-each body word keeps compiling

column1: def g fn [[xs:List] [Any] [def n 10 each [n add] xs]] end g [1 2]
column3: a fn-local VALUE def read by the body is a lexical capture, not a compile failure

column1: # §8  chained forward application of Function params — the compose family.
#     `f (g x)` inside a fn body applies the inner param fn at the paren
#     and the outer param fn over its result — the canonical HOF chain.
#     A live MISCOMPILE until 2026-08-02 (the whole-frame replay's flat
#     window lost the paren structure and compiled the RET count error),
#     then a compile failure; GRADUATED 2026-08-03 by the Stage-G single-arg
#     increment: the leading one-arg apply `(g x)` records the same
#     RecordDynApply event as the trailing spelling `(x g)` (the two
#     collections converge at one argument), so the inner group collapses
#     to an event and the outer apply rides the single-applicable RetReplay
#     body tail. These rows hold BOTH engines to the chain through the
#     differential gate (native pins: lang/go/bytecode_chained_apply_test.go).
def compose fn [[f:Function g:Function x:Integer] [Integer] [f (g x)]] compose ([a:Integer] => [a mul 2]) ([b:Integer] => [b add 3]) 4
column3: the canonical compose: outer param fn applied to the inner param fn's result

column1: def twice fn [[f:Function x:Integer] [Integer] [f (f x)]] twice ([n:Integer] => [n add 1]) 5
column3: self-composition — the same fn value read twice, applied at two depths

column1: def stage fn [[f:Function x:Integer] [Integer] [def r (f x) f r]] stage ([n:Integer] => [n add 1]) 5
column3: the def-split idiom: the apply seats in a def, the tail applies over the bound name (replayIsBodyTail's windowReadsID arm)

column1: def tds fn [[g:Function x:Integer] [Integer] [def r (x g) g r]] tds ([n:Integer] => [n add 1]) 5
column3: the trailing-spelling def-split twin — same seating through the trailing RecordDynApply event

column1: def chain fn [[a:Function b:Function s:Integer][Integer][def r1 (a s) def r2 (b r1) r2]] chain ([n:Integer] => [n add 1]) ([n:Integer] => [n mul 10]) 4
column3: CHAINED def-split (NUR087, fixed 2026-08-24): the second def calls through a Function param with the FIRST def's dynamic binding as its argument. The collapse used to require a non-dynamic argument, so this window stalled the pending def and every later read of r2 raised a false undefined_word — declining a program both engines run

column1: # §9  gradual-Any into a multi-overload user fn with DIFFERING arm returns.
#     The checker cannot statically commit an arm, and until 2026-08-03 one
#     recorded output type would lie for the unselected arm, so the shape
#     declined ("ambiguous dispatch, no poly re-match"). The §8.2(3)
#     return-join graduation records the JOIN of the arms' returns (a
#     dynamic carrier at the arms' common ancestor) and the VM's
#     OpCallUserPoly re-match selects the concrete arm — whichever arm
#     runs, downstream typing rides the join, never one arm's unproven
#     commitment (pins: lang/go/bytecode_poly_join_test.go).
def id fn [[x:Any] [Any] [x]] def g fn [[a:Integer] [Integer] [1] [a:String] [String] ['s']] g (id 5)
column3: differing arm returns: Integer arm selected at runtime

column1: def id fn [[x:Any] [Any] [x]] def g fn [[a:Integer] [Integer] [1] [a:String] [String] ['s']] g (id 'x')
column3: differing arm returns: String arm selected at runtime

column1: # §10 canon over a fn value — content, name-independent (NUR031).
#     GRADUATED 2026-08-27 (Stage 3) out of
#     lang/spec/frontier/frontier-nur031-fn-eq.tsv. `canon` only READS a
#     fn value's content, never invokes it, so it declares CompileReadsFn
#     and the value rides as an ordinary const operand. That
#     name-independence is what deq rides on: the binding a function was
#     reached through is not part of what it is.
def f fn x:Integer [Integer] [x add 1] canon (f/v)
column3: canon renders the anonymous fn literal — no `fn f`, because the name is how it was reached

column1: def f fn x:Integer [Integer] [x add 1] def a (f/v) (canon (a/v)) eq (canon (f/v))
column3: so one function under two names has ONE canon — the name-independence deq rides on

column1: # §11 UNDER-APPLICATION: a window WIDER than the callee's arity.
#     GRADUATED 2026-08-28 (Stage 3) out of
#     lang/spec/frontier/frontier-hof-audit.tsv §9c. The interpreter
#     applies the callee to the values nearest it and leaves the deeper
#     ones in the residual; the compiled lane now does the same, because
#     RecordDynApply reports how many window values the lowered apply
#     CONSUMES and the collapse site removes only that suffix. The arity
#     is sound by construction — a closure unit with a known param count,
#     or a single-signature concrete callee — so a factory whose branches
#     return different arities, or an overloaded callee, never reaches the
#     trim. The narrower window (fewer args than the arity) is the
#     opposite shape and still declines: the interpreter leaves the fn
#     UNAPPLIED, which nothing here models.
def mk fn a:Integer Function [(fn b:Integer Integer [add a b])] end (1 2 (mk 4))
column3: a 1-arg closure under a 2-wide window: the adder takes the top value, the deeper 1 survives

column1: def mk fn a:Integer Function [(fn b:Integer Integer [add a b])] end (1 2 3 (mk 4))
column3: …and two deeper values survive, in order

column1: def add2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][add a b]]  (9 1 2 add2/v)
column3: a CONCRETE 2-arg callee under a 3-wide window — the survivor stays BELOW the result, the order the compiled lane used to get backwards

column1: def mk2 fn [[n:Integer] [Function] [([a:Integer b:Integer] => [a add b add n])]]  (1 2 3 (mk2 10))
column3: a 2-arg closure under a 3-wide window consumes the top two

column1: # §12 RETURN CONTRACT UNDER APPLICATION: an applied fn value's DECLARED
#     return is enforced by whichever engine runs it.
#     A stamped fn-value unit compiles COUNT-AGNOSTIC — compileStoredFnUnit
#     goes through compileClosureBody with bodyOut 0, so CompiledFn.Returns is
#     empty and its RET enforces nothing. That is right for the unit (the
#     callback seam wants the raw residual) and wrong for an APPLICATION,
#     where the interpreter's __RC runs inside the CallBoru the island reaches.
#     Until the Apply kernel carried the applied value's contract into the
#     frame it enters, the first row below answered 'str' compiled and raised
#     interpreted — a silent wrong answer, which is the class this project
#     ranks strictly above a compile failure. The violation is only visible at RUN
#     time (the body returns its `n:Any` param), so no static pass can stand
#     in for the runtime contract.
def bad fn [[n:Any][Integer][n]] end def mk fn [[][Function][bad/v]] end ((mk) 'str')
column3: an applied fn value's declared return TYPE is enforced on both engines

column1: def okr fn [[n:Any][Integer][n]] end def mk fn [[][Function][okr/v]] end ((mk) 7)
column3: …and a conforming value passes through unchanged

column1: # §13 RETURN CONTRACT ON THE CALLBACK PATH: the same enforcement, one seam
#     down. A callback fn value handed to a higher-order word (`each`,
#     `fold`, `filter`, …) runs as a CLOSURE, not through Apply — the VM
#     enters the stamped unit directly at invokeClosureOn. The unit itself
#     is compiled COUNT-AGNOSTIC on purpose (the callback seam wants the raw
#     residual, and the WORD's count convention is not the CALLBACK's type
#     contract), so the contract cannot ride on the unit: keying it there
#     changes the FnAnalysisKey and a conforming `fold f/v` islands. It
#     rides on the closure VALUE instead — Program.ClosureRet, keyed by the
#     pc of the OpPushClosure that built it — and is checked against the
#     values the body actually produced. Before that, the first row below
#     answered [1 2] compiled and raised interpreted: a silent wrong answer.
def cbad fn [[n:Integer][Boolean][n]] end [1 2] each cbad/v
column3: a callback fn's declared return is enforced on the closure path too

column1: def cokr fn [[n:Integer][Boolean][n gt 0]] end [1 2] each cokr/v
column3: …and a conforming callback passes through unchanged

column1: def clit fn [[n:Integer][Boolean][1]] end [1 2] each clit/v
column3: …and a callback whose body is a bare LITERAL is held to it too — no application to strand an operand, no param read to surface a stand-in, so the concrete residual IS the return

column1: def cstr fn [[n:Integer][Boolean]['s']] end [1 2] each cstr/v
column3: a literal body of any leaf type, not just the Integer one that surfaced it

column1: def cfit fn [[n:Integer][Integer][1]] end [1 2] each cfit/v
column3: …and a CONFORMING literal body is not rejected, so the arm above is not just a blanket compile failure of literal bodies

column1: def flitp fn [[1] [1] [dup drop]] end 99
column3: a literal PARAM pattern widens to its parent for the generalised body analysis, so the residual must NOT be measured against a literal RETURN pattern — `flitp 1` is 1 on both engines, and checking it against `1` reported a mismatch that does not exist

column1: # §7  a bare read of a Function-typed PARAM is a CALL (NUR123; ruled 2026-08-15,
#     ADR-016: a bare name is a call, `/v` asks for the value, arity never
#     changes how a function behaves). The compiled lane re-steps the read as
#     the WORD (CompiledFn.DynFrameWords) — graduated 2026-09-05 from
#     frontier-fnparam-deref.tsv.
def nought fn [[] [Integer] [7]] def grab fn [[f:Function] [Any] [f]] typeof (grab nought)
column3: arity-0 Function param read bare: the bare name is a call, so it APPLIES (7 -> Integer) on both lanes

column1: def dbl fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [n mul 2]] def hold fn [[c:Function] [Any] [c]] typeof (hold dbl)
column3: arity-1 Function param read bare with no argument: the call RAISES on both lanes
